The Music Machine sits on a simple premise. Though it delves deeper through its concepts. Like The Moon Sliver, this game is a walking sim that aims to get you to explore. To listen and think. To identify and digest. It's a simple treasure we often take for granted. You start by hearing the characters out, learning a bit about them. Then you learn more as time goes on. You never have the full story as much as you'd like to. But that's not what's important. What is important is that you understand what you are witnessing now. 

The Music Machine is a nightmare. A set of worlds without practical meaning. Creation for the sake of creation. The why is to imitate. Cheaply and without purpose. The worlds displayed in the Music Machine are brutalist and disgusting. A vile misinterpretation of what it means to build something. A divinity shrouded in madness, but not malice. Crude, misunderstood, lonely. Adolescent. 

If you played The Moon Sliver and want more from that same universe, or to understand that one a little bit better, then this game is for you. I do recommend it if you want something quick to play that will get you thinking about the deeper connotations and meanings behind it all. Excellent work from David Szymanski like always.

[H1]Un racconto surreale[/H1]

The Music Machine mi ha preso in un modo raro. Lo stile surreale è meraviglioso: non è solo “strano per essere strano”, ma costruisce un’immaginario coerente, inquieto, a tratti quasi ipnotico, che ti fa sentire costantemente fuori posto nel modo giusto.

La cosa che mi ha colpito di più, però, è la storia. È scritta davvero bene: non ti imbocca, ma ti lascia mettere insieme i pezzi e quando capisci dove sta andando, l’impatto è doppio. I dialoghi sono uno dei punti forti: asciutti, taglienti quando serve, e capaci di raccontare tantissimo con poco. Il rapporto tra i personaggi è volutamente scomodo e “storto”, ma proprio per questo funziona: ti spinge a riflettere, ti mette a disagio, poi ti sorprende con momenti in cui intravedi sfumature che non ti aspettavi.

Anche il mood è speciale: quella sensazione di essere trascinato in qualcosa di più grande, di non avere mai terreno stabile sotto i piedi, è resa benissimo. E la spiegazione finale (senza fare spoiler) è esattamente il tipo di chiusura che adoro: non banale, non buttata lì, ma una rivelazione che dà senso a ciò che hai visto e ti lascia con quella soddisfazione strana, un po’ amara, un po’ affascinata.

E sì: è un walking simulator, ma per me è proprio l’esempio di come questo genere possa essere fatto bene. Dopo aver giocato The Moon Silver, che personalmente non ho apprezzato, qui ho trovato esattamente quello che mi era mancato: una narrazione più incisiva, un ritmo più coinvolgente, un’atmosfera più curata e soprattutto una scrittura che non sembra “solo un’idea interessante”, ma una storia che sa dove vuole arrivare e ci arriva lasciandoti qualcosa. Se come me in The Moon Silver avevi trovato dei limiti, The Music Machine sembra quasi la risposta: prende quel tipo di esperienza e la rende più densa, più memorabile, più significativa.

Consigliato a chi ama l’horror surreale, le storie che ti scavano un po’ dentro e i giochi che puntano su atmosfera e scrittura invece che su action e jumpscare gratuiti. Io l’ho adorato.

Kilka razy na tej stronce zdarzyło mi się wspomnieć o Davidzie Szymańskim, na moim radarze umieścił go kapitalny Dusk, ale nie była to jego pierwsza produkcja, poza boomer shooterami robi on bowiem również powolne horrory/walking simy. Już jakiś czas temu spróbowałem jego pierwszej gry The Moon Silver i srogo się zawiodłem. Dziś opowiem wam o tym czego doświadczyłem w jego drugiej grze. 

The Music Machine od razu przyciąga uwagę screenami. Binarna kolorystyka i duży kontrast przyciąga oko. Jeśli jednak się temu przyjrzymy to jest to praca prostych shaderów nałożonych na podobnie nieskomplikowane modele. W tym wszystkim kryje się też moim zdaniem esencja całej gry. Niewiele elementów, które pracują razem w celu osiągnięcia efektu większego niż suma części. 

Pomimo swojej prostoty, grafika buduje kapitalny klimat eksplorowania obcego świata. To jedna z płaszczyzn opowieści The Music Machine i low poly modele działają zaskakująco dobrze. Te obce światy natomiast są eksplorowane przez dwójkę bohaterów, a ich relacja jest drugą płaszczyzną historii. Chłop gadający z babą przez radio to klasyk walking simów, ale tu mamy pewien twist. Otóż gramy duchem dorosłego mężczyzny, który opętał ciało nastolatki i próbuje się na niej zemścić, za co? Tego nie będę zdradzał. Mogę tylko powiedzieć, że dla mnie opowieść była bardzo ciekawa. 

Gameplayowo jest to czysty walking sim, oferujący może co nieco zagadek, ale na tyle prostych, że nie ma co o nich więcej gadać. Co jednak ważne nie ma tu upierdliwego badziewia, które mogłoby nas wyrwać z doświadczania tej klimatycznej opowieści  

Zanim jednak gorąco wam grę polecę muszę jeszcze dodać standardowy disclaimer że to gra narracyjna, w którą gramy dla klimatu i historii, nie ma tu gameplayu.  Te dwa jednak mnie oczarowały. Daję znaczek jakości, być może trochę na wyrost, ale to mój folwark i to ja tu jestem sołtysem. Dajcie szanse jeśli lubicie gatunek, szczególnie, że gra jest tania, krótka i od bardzo rigczowego twórcy.

[h2]Стилистика[/h2] 
Да согласен, если увидеть скрины из игры в первый раз покажется вырвиглазной. Но так только в начале. Поиграв пару минут привыкаешь к оформлению и в целом. Выглядит даже стильно. Мне понравилось, тем более подобных игр не так уж и много. 

[h2]Сюжет[/h2] 
Тут он есть, хотя забывается он очень быстро. Не сказать, что он какой-то откровенный, но Дэвид снова перегружает текст метафорами просто потому что. Это не раздражает, ведь я например узнал много новых английских слов. Кстати рекомендую поиграть в игры Дэвида тем, кто изучает инглиш. Да сложно, но можно обнаружить очень много новых слов для себя и подтянуть хотя бы словарный запас. 

Мне понравилась идея о призраке, который сидит в девочке. В целом интересно наблюдать за их взаимодействием. Но иногда прям полный стыд читать их перепалки. Кто понял тот понял. 

Концовки кстати две. До второй можно чисто логически додуматься, она относительно не линейно получается. 

[h2]Итог[/h2]
Мне понравилось. Выглядит как личный прогресс автора, не тривиальная стилистика и средний сюжет с кучей метафор о жизни и смерти. Проходится быстро, но забывается еще быстрее.

REVIEW #105
The Music Machine
----------

David Szymanski has a knack for creating very interesting stories and characters with a viewpoint that may different from that of the average person, and in my opinion, The Music Machine is one of the best examples of this that I've come across.

TMM is a uniquely-styled, story-driven adventure title that plays out more like an experience in exploration than a game. Yes, I'm saying that it's a walking simulator... but it's a really good one. It's also a short game that will take about 1 to 2 hours of the player's time from start to finish, so it easily avoids overstaying its welcome and yet doesn't feel too brief.

The Music Machine's strongest points are its story and style. Its tale and the surrounding characters are all interesting and unique, and I enjoyed learning everything that I could through dialog and reading notes found around the environments. Speaking of the game's locations, all of the locales are very odd and fascinating to explore, almost making me feel like I was experiencing someone's dreams at points.

[spoiler]It's worth mentioning that TMM's story ties into other games created by the developer, including The Moon Sliver. However, while it may be necessary to play or read about those other titles to fully understand the tale offered here, I didn't find doing that necessary to essentially understand what was happening exclusively in the immediate world of this game.[/spoiler]

The Music Machine's graphics are rendered monochromatically with low-resolution (yet high-quality) textures, and every area uses a different base color, helping to give each world its own distinct feel while exploring. Personally, I enjoy the game's graphical style as it seems to give its environments a surreal and dream-like quality. The sound production is also very well done, leaning more on environmental ambient sounds than music. However, what music and injected background ambiances that are here are really good and are appropriately engaging without feel overwhelming or too skeletal in their integration into the overall experience.

TMM isn't perfect, of course, and it may not be for everyone. Other players have voiced that the story was either uninteresting or hard to understand, and while my opinion doesn't align with that, it is a complaint that I've seen occur fairly often, and I did personally feel that some parts of the story felt underdeveloped or "tacked on". Outside of that aspect of the game, other issues that I feel are worth mentioning include that it sometimes feels a little vague regarding how to advance. I found myself wandering around on one or two occasions in an attempt to figure out what I needed to do next, although I acknowledge that I never found myself needing to check a guide. In my wanderings, however, I did find that the monochromatic visual style did make it hard to optically determine what steeper inclines in the landscape I could or couldn't simply walk up without coming to a dead stop and having to find another way around. Also, some of the shadowing can look a little glitchy and unnatural in a small handful of areas, especially where tree branches are being moved by wind.

Still, I feel that The Music Machine is worth picking up if you're in the mood for exploring interesting and bizarre worlds all tied together by a unique story. $5 USD (which is the current price) may be a little steep for some players, especially considering that it is a pretty short game, and I suggest that those players wait until it goes on sale as I did. Regardless, I can confidently say that I'm quite happy with my purchase and to have this title in my Steam library. I've thoroughly enjoyed multiple play-throughs of TMM, and I confidently predict that I'll be coming back for another one in the near future.

Another short horror exploration game improving on David Szymanski's previous titles Fingerbones and The Moon Sliver. Solid minimalist sound and visuals are to be expected at this point, though The Music Machine opts for a more unique and striking monochromatic style which works really well.  It's unsettling and creepy without cheap scares, has dialog and a real-time story that flow well, and optional exploration and organic decisions that affect the game's ending.

My only mechanical complaint is that the "hold M1 to examine, release to interact" system is silly - there's no reason I wouldn't want to examine something, so it just means I have to spend the whole game running around with M1 held down. I'm not 100% a fan of the lore expansion, as it undermines some of the mystery and potential metaphorical interpretations of The Moon Sliver, but that's purely subjective.

The story is the weird part for me: [spoiler]Haley (13f) hangs out with Quintin (34m) because they're both lonely outcasts. She makes an advance, he shuts her down hard, she is hurt and lies to her father saying she was molested, dad kills Quintin, Quintin's ghost possesses her seeking revenge. Based on the player's choices he either finds a horrific way of doing so, or when faced with the reality of his revenge realizes he's not willing to go through with it. Based on both of their dialog, Quintin was entirely in the right and Haley was being childish, got him *killed*, and didn't seem too sorry about it until her own life was in jeopardy. I'm not really sure what the point of their weird "relationship" was. The best interpretation I can come up with is that in contrast to the Spindle Men's horrifically logical, literal, and utilitarian view of the universe, human interaction is illogical, messy, and emotional. Their lives and relationship (romantic or not) were messy before death, messy after, and even though Quintin is apparently completely justified in killing Haley, maybe he won't, even if he doesn't forgive her.[/spoiler] If nothing else, it made me think for a bit.

100% worth the $ and time spent.
